newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania March inflation seen easing to 10-12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania March inflation seen easing to 10-12 pct.

text.p: Romania's monthly inflation is expected to ease to 10-12 percent in March from a 45-month peak of 18.8 percent in February, when energy and food prices were freed, a central bank (BNR) official said on Monday.
"According to our provisional estimates, March inflation will likely be at about 10 to 12 percent," BNR spokesman Adrian Vasilescu told a news conference.

BNR monetary policy manager Ion Dragulin said the March forecast was slightly above a previous estimate of 9.0 to 10 percent. He said the new forecast took into consideration a slower than initially planned pace of price liberalisation.
Romania's centrist coalition, which replaced ex-communists in last year's elections, freed prices for utilities, energy and staples in mid-February as part of a broad reform programme.
Year-on-year inflation jumped to 105.4 percent in February from 76.3 percent in January, with a two-month consumer price increase of 35 percent.
Official forecasts put year-on-year inflation forecasts for year-end at about 90 percent. The government aims to cut monthly inflation to about 2.0 percent by December.

An International Monetary Fund mission was due to arrive in Bucharest on Monday to monitor progress on the programme ahead of a decision at the IMF board meeting this month on resuming credits to the Balkan country.
